# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 20 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 20 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_020_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 12

**1** "Those from the third mountain — full of thorns and briars — who are they?" "These are believers, but some are wealthy and some are deeply involved in business. The briars represent the wealthy; the thorns represent those caught up in various commercial dealings. These do not keep company with God's servants — they are choked by their business dealings and their wealth, cut off from the righteous." **2** "Some of them do give to the poor, while others keep everything they have. Those who give receive salvation; those who keep everything are rejected." **3** "Those from the fourth mountain — thorny at the top but green below — these are the double-minded, those who are not entirely righteous. They have faith, but also great wealth. For the most part they are unrighteous, yet they have some capacity for repentance because their green portions are not entirely lifeless." **4** "Those from the fifth mountain — green grass but rugged — these are believers and upright, but they are obstinate and self-willed. They want to understand everything, yet they truly understand nothing." **5** "Because of their stubbornness and empty conceit they quarrel with one another; they think they have mastered everything but are the most ignorant of all. Their foolish arrogance has made them evil, and they have fallen away from the truth." **6** "Nevertheless there is repentance for them, since they are not wicked but foolish and lacking discernment. If they repent they will live to God; but if they do not repent they will share the company of women who have done them harm."

---

*LOGOS note: "double-minded" (dipsychos) reappears as a category here — those who try to hold both faith and wealth. The fifth mountain's problem is intellectual pride combined with practical ignorance.*
